# LearnHarness Git Back up and sync your [LearnHarness](https://github.com/amosblomqvist/learnharness) learning data with Git: sessions, knowledge graph, flashcards and settings. [![CI](https://github.com/heohlee/learnharness-git/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/heohlee/learnharness-git/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Security](https://github.com/heohlee/learnharness-git/actions/workflows/security.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/heohlee/learnharness-git/actions/workflows/security.yml)
A [LearnHarness](https://github.com/amosblomqvist/learnharness) community plugin, inspired by obsidian-git. It turns the learning data folder into a Git repository and keeps it backed up on a remote you own: commit, pull and push on a schedule or with one button. It uses the `git` installed on your computer, with your own SSH keys or credential helper, and it handles merge conflicts without ever leaving broken JSON in your learning records. ## Features - **Git view**: backup status, Sync now and pending changes (stage, unstage, diff, commit). Click "Backed up …" to open Git History. The change viewer takes only a relative path and follows it through the real filesystem from the learning-data folder: an absolute path, or one that leaves the folder through `..` or a symlink, shows an error instead of a diff.

- **Git History**: every commit with its hash, file count and time, expandable to its files. Shows the author only if it isn't you.

- **Automatic sync**: commit, pull and push every N minutes; pull on startup. - **Connect a remote**: set the URL in Settings; before the first push, flags files that may hold secrets, including in the history. A URL is refused, with a reminder to use SSH keys or a credential helper, when it carries a password, when its user name or a query or fragment parameter names a credential (`token`, `password`, `pwd`, `secret`, `api-key`), or when it holds a known token prefix such as `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `glpat-` or `glpat_` — plain or percent-encoded. This check is a heuristic: a token with none of those markers is not recognised, so keep credentials out of the URL yourself. - **Second computer**: clone an existing backup; replaced local files go to `.learnharness-git-backup/`. - **Clean clone failure**: a clone that cannot write every file fails instead of reporting success, removes only the files it wrote itself, keeps or restores what was already there, and can be retried. - **Merge conflicts**: resolved automatically (newest wins, the other is backed up) or per file (Local / Remote, with diff). A session you deleted in the app is not brought back by sync, deletions survive on both sides, and you are never asked about the app's own files; the notice names what was kept. - **Valid JSON only**: invalid JSON is never committed. - **Safe with your Git work**: never touches a merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert you started. - **Clear auth errors**: suggests `gh auth setup-git` or an SSH URL. - **Keyboard actions**: commit, sync, pull and push. ## Requirements - LearnHarness 0.6.1 or newer (desktop app). - `git` 2.31 or newer on the `PATH`. - For a remote: SSH keys, or HTTPS with a credential helper (for GitHub: `gh auth login && gh auth setup-git`). The plugin never asks for a password. - Install paths 2 and 3 also need Node.js 24 or newer and npm. ## Install Find the plugins folder in **Settings → Community plugins** (by default on Linux: `~/.config/LearnHarness/data/plugins`). ### 1. Prebuilt package (recommended) Download `learnharness-git-.zip` from the [releases](https://github.com/heohlee/learnharness-git/releases). It already contains the `learnharness-git/` folder: extract it directly into the plugins folder, so that `/learnharness-git/dist/manifest.json` exists. To update: replace only `learnharness-git/dist/` with the new one (keep `learnharness-git/data/`, which holds the plugin settings), then restart LearnHarness. ### 2. From source, inside the plugins folder ```sh git clone https://github.com/heohlee/learnharness-git.git "/learnharness-git" cd "/learnharness-git" npm ci npm run build ``` To update: `git pull && npm ci && npm run build`, then restart LearnHarness. The clone has its own `.git`, so the plugin keeps `plugins/learnharness-git/` out of your backup (in `.git/info/exclude`, on this computer only), and its settings in `data/` are not backed up. The same applies to any plugin installed with `git clone`. If v0.1.0 already committed the folder, remove it from the backup once with `git rm --cached plugins/learnharness-git` in the learning data folder, then commit. ### 3. From a separate checkout (development) ```sh git clone https://github.com/heohlee/learnharness-git.git cd learnharness-git npm ci npm run install:local -- "" ``` `install:local` builds and replaces only the installed `dist/`. Restart LearnHarness to load code changes. ### Turn it on **Settings → Community plugins → Refresh plugins**, then turn on **Enable Git**. **Git** appears in the sidebar. ## Usage 1. Open **Git** in the sidebar. 2. First computer: press **Initialize repository**. Second computer: press **Clone from remote** and paste the backup URL, then restart LearnHarness. 3. In **Settings → Git → Remote URL**, paste the URL of an empty private repository (for example `git@github.com:you/learning-data.git`) and confirm **Connect and push**. 4. Press **Sync now**, or set **Auto sync interval** and turn on **Pull and push after each automatic commit**. **Initialize repository** adds a `.gitignore` and a `.gitattributes` for the learning data if they don't exist. Existing ones are never changed. The `.gitattributes` makes graph ledgers changed on two computers merge instead of conflicting. Merging graph ledgers line by line is safe for records both sides added, but not for a record one side deleted. Before merging, the plugin reads the ledgers and the chats themselves. A record this computer removed stays removed while the remote's new records are kept, and a session the app deleted here stays deleted even if the remote edited it: sync applies this itself, so no user choice is required. A discarded remote version is saved first under `.learnharness-git-backup/`, which stays out of the repository. Because the files are read directly, an existing `graph/*.jsonl merge=union` attribute cannot hide a deletion, and the plugin never changes your `.gitattributes`. The same rule runs the other way: a deletion made on the other computer also stays deleted here, even when this computer only added records; the version it replaced is kept as `.local` next to the upstream one under `.learnharness-git-backup/`. A deletion the remote did not touch, and ledgers both sides only added to, merge as before. If the file sync must rewrite already has uncommitted changes, sync stops and names it instead of overwriting your edit: commit or discard it, then pull again.
What they contain ```gitignore # Automatic graph copies: Git already keeps every version of graph/. graph-backup-*/ # Usage log of the built-in plugins: nothing reads it. core-plugin-data/*/usage.jsonl # Community plugin code; keep only each plugin's data/ (its settings). plugins/*/* !plugins/*/data/ # Graph layout: rewritten whenever the graph is opened, and recomputed if missing. graph/positions.json ``` ```gitattributes graph/*.jsonl merge=union ```
## Configuration **Settings → Git**:

| Setting | Default | Description | | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Auto sync interval (minutes) | `0` | Commit every N minutes; `0` turns it off. | | Pull and push after each automatic commit | off | Needs an upstream branch. | | Pull when LearnHarness starts | off | Pull once at startup. | | Commit message template | `learnharness backup: {{date}}` | For automatic commits and when the message box is empty. | | Conflicts | Resolve automatically | Newest wins for ordinary files, deletions are kept, the other side is backed up. Or **Ask me** to pick Local / Remote per file. | | Remote URL | (none) | `origin`; saving it pushes after you confirm. No passwords or tokens in the URL. | ## Privacy The plugin runs Git on your learning data folder only. Everything in that folder that your `.gitignore` does not exclude (sessions, the knowledge graph, flashcards, settings) is committed and pushed to the remote you choose: use a private repository. Provider API keys live outside that folder and are never read or pushed. The plugin stores only its own settings, in `learnharness-git/data/settings.json` next to its code. It contacts no service other than your Git remote. ## Development ```sh npm ci npm run coverage # tests with an 85% line, branch and function minimum npm run typecheck npm run lint npm run package # releases/learnharness-git-.zip, the prebuilt package ``` ## License [AGPL-3.0](LICENSE)

releases.notes:
## Fixes

- A session deleted in LearnHarness no longer comes back after syncing with another computer. The plugin resolves that incoming change itself, keeps the deletion on both sides, and saves every discarded version under `.learnharness-git-backup/`.
- Sync refuses to rewrite a learning file that has uncommitted changes and names it, instead of overwriting the edit.
- A clone that cannot write every file now fails with the missing paths instead of reporting success, restores what was there, and can be retried in the same folder.
- A failed clone removes only the files it wrote itself, so a file another program created during the attempt survives.
- The change viewer only reads inside the learning data folder, including when a path tries to leave through a symlink and `..`.
- A remote URL carrying credentials is refused before any Git call, including percent-encoded forms, and GitLab `glpat-` tokens are recognised again.
- The notice after an automatic conflict resolution now states the rule that was actually applied instead of always claiming the newest version won.

Full changelog: https://github.com/heohlee/learnharness-git/compare/v0.1.1...v0.1.2
